messages.content: What is the best month to visit Hawaii?

function.name: get_average_monthly_temperature

message.content:
The “best” month to visit Hawaii depends on what you’re looking for—weather, crowds, price, or activities—but most travelers agree that **late spring (April–June) and early fall (September–November)** strike the best balance.

| Season | Typical Weather | Crowds & Prices | Why It’s Great |
|--------|-----------------|-----------------|----------------|
| **Late Spring (Apr–Jun)** | Warm, sunny days (70–80 °F / 21–27 °C), light rain showers | Moderate crowds, lower rates than summer | Ideal for beach‑time, hiking, and cultural events; the islands feel lively but not overcrowded. |
| **Early Fall (Sep–Nov)** | Warm, sunny days (70–80 °F / 21–27 °C), occasional showers | Similar to late spring – moderate crowds, good deals | Great for surfing, whale watching (Oct–Nov), and enjoying the islands after the peak‑summer rush. |
| **Peak Summer (Jul–Aug)** | Hot, humid (80–90 °F / 27–32 °C), occasional afternoon showers | High crowds, higher accommodation costs | Perfect if you’re after the busiest beach parties and water‑park fun, but expect crowds and pricier stays. |
| **Winter (Dec–Feb)** | Cooler, drier (60–70 °F / 15–21 °C), occasional rain | Lower crowds, cheaper rates | Good for whale watching (Dec–Feb), but some beaches may be cooler and windier. |

### Quick Weather Snapshot (Hawaii – average daily highs)

| Month | Avg. High (°F) | Avg. High (°C) |
|-------|----------------|----------------|
| Jan   | 78             | 26            |
| Feb   | 79             | 26            |
| Mar   | 80             | 27            |
| Apr   | 81             | 27            |
| May   | 82             | 28            |
| Jun   | 83             | 28            |
| Jul   | 84             | 29            |
| Aug   | 84             | 29            |
| Sep   | 83             | 28            |
| Oct   | 82             | 28            |
| Nov   | 81             | 27            |
| Dec   | 79             | 26            |

*(These averages come from NOAA’s climate data for Honolulu.)*

---

#### Bottom line

If you want **pleasant temperatures, fewer crowds, and better rates**, book for **May, June, September, or October**. If you’re okay with higher prices and don’t mind crowds, **July or August** will still give you great beach vibes and plenty of activities. And if you’re a whale‑watcher, plan for **December–February**.
